newsitem.title: USA: Holocaust survivor to negotiate with Germans.
newsitem.headline: Holocaust survivor to negotiate with Germans.

text.p: A delegation of Jewish leaders headed for critical talks on reparations in Germany next week will have, for the first time, an East European Holocaust survivor as one of its negotiators, Jewish sources said on Wednesday.

The sources said that Latvian Jewish leader Alexander Bergman will be part of the team headed by World Jewish Congress Secretary General Israel Singer that is seeking German reparations for East European Holocaust survivors.
The Germans have paid billions of dollars in reparations to Western European Holocaust survivors but nothing to Jews in Eastern Europe or the former Soviet Union.
Only 82 Holocaust survivors remain in Latvia, which had a pre-war Jewish population of 100,000.

The German government has come under fire for its refusal to compensate East European survivors even while it is paying tens of thousands of SS and Nazi police veterans in East Europe and other countries outside of Germany.

Recently published figures showed that last year so-called disability pensions were paid to 1.1 million veterans and dependants of Nazi Germany's armed forces, totaling some 13 billion marks ($7.7 billion).

A majority of the seven-member Jewish delegation will be composed of Holocaust survivors, the sources said. It will meet next week in Bonn with Chancellor Helmut Kohl's top administrative aide and members of the German Finance Ministry.
Other issues to be discussed are restrictions currently placed on Holocaust survivors receiving reparations.
In order to receive payments, a person must have spent at least six months in a concentration camp or 18 months in a ghetto and have an annual income under $14,000 per year.

The American Jewish Committee said it planned to publish a series of full-page newspaper ads on Sunday reprinting a letter to Kohl from 82 U.S. senators urging Germany to change its stand on reparations.
